author: Esbern, archivist

#The Carving

Alduin's Wall, in the old Blades temple, shows the World-Eater brought down from the sky. The ancient Nords did not kill him. The carving is very clear about this: he falls, and then he is simply not there.

What brought him down was a Shout. The wall shows it as a spear of light from three mouths at once.

#Why It Cannot Be Taught

A Shout is a way of thinking, spoken. The dragons think in their own tongue, and to them, death is a foreign word. They cannot conceive of their own ending.

The mortals who made this Shout put that idea, mortality, into dragon words. A dragon hearing it is forced to understand it, and for a moment, cannot fly.

#A Fear

The Greybeards will not teach it, and the dragons cannot. I believe the only way to learn it now is to witness it, somehow, at the moment it was first spoken.

That moment is long gone. Unless an Elder Scroll were to be read at the very place where time itself was wounded. Which is, of course, madness. I have written it down anyway.
